privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.section0:
Privacy Policy

flow-otter.com respects your privacy and is committed to protecting your personal data in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (General Data Protection Regulation), in force since 24 May 2016 and applicable from 25 May 2018.

This privacy policy applies to all visitors to the flow-otter.com website.
privacy.section1:
Introduction

This policy describes how flow-otter.com processes personal data when interacting with flow-otter.com for our services or simply for browsing our website. It also aims to inform users about their legal rights regarding privacy and the protection offered by the legal system. We invite you to read this privacy policy carefully in order to be informed about our use of your personal data. If you have any questions or wish to exercise a privacy right, please follow the instructions in this privacy policy. Please contact flow-otter.com with any questions about privacy at the data controller's email address: info@flow-otter.com.
privacy.section2:
Personal data we may collect

Personal data, or personal information, is information relating to any individual from which their identity can be ascertained. This therefore excludes data from which the user's identity has been removed (anonymous data). We collect a range of information about our customers. This personal data falls into the following categories.

Identifying data: first name, surname and, if the user communicates with us via social media, this category also includes the username used on such social media.
Contact details: postal address, telephone numbers, email addresses, billing address.
User identification codes or keys.
Data relating to personal characteristics: date of birth, gender, nationality.
Operational data: this includes information relating to payments to and from the customer, as well as additional information relating to the products and services purchased from us.

We do not collect sensitive data about you (including data revealing racial or ethnic origin, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life, sexual orientation, political opinions, health information, and genetic and biometric data). Furthermore, we do not collect judicial data relating to you.
privacy.section3:
How personal data is collected

Below is a list of the different methods we use to collect user data.

Direct interaction.
The user decides to provide their identification, contact and financial details by filling in a form or communicating such data by post, telephone, e-mail, chat or social media.
The personal data provided by the user is included when:

They request an offer for our goods/services;
They submit requests or solicit information; They request an appointment; They submit a CV from our website;
They contact us via social media;
They subscribe to our Newsletter.
privacy.section4:
How we use your personal data

We use personal data within the limits of the law. In general, we use data in the following circumstances:

If we need to perform a contract that is being concluded or has already been concluded with you. For example, issuing an invoice for goods/services provided to you.
If it is necessary to pursue our legitimate interests (or those of third parties), provided that the user's interests and fundamental rights do not override them.
If we need to comply with obligations imposed by laws or regulations.
In general, the legal basis on which we base the processing of your personal data does not include your consent, except in cases expressly provided for by law, such as for sending certain direct marketing communications.
In cases where the legal basis is based on consent, you have the right to withdraw your consent at any time.

For more information, please compare the legal bases on which we rely for the processing of personal data with the legal basis on which we rely for the processing of personal data.
privacy.section5:
The legal basis on which we process personal data

You are aware that we may process your personal data on different legal bases, depending on the specific purpose of the data use. Our decision-making process is not automated. We invite you to send us any questions you may have in this regard. For questions regarding privacy, please refer to the section How to contact flow-otter.com.
privacy.section6:
Advertising, marketing and user preferences in communications

With your specific consent, we may use direct marketing strategies via email, telephone, SMS or post. For example, you may receive our newsletter via your email address.
We make every effort to ensure that our website clearly indicates our activities and the type of messages sent to you, both when you decide to receive our newsletter and when you fill in the contact form.
You can change your mind at any time and decide to unsubscribe.
privacy.section7:
Cookies

By using the website, users consent to the use of cookies in accordance with this policy. If the user does not consent to the use of cookies in this way, they must set their browser appropriately or not use the website. If the user decides to disable cookies, this may affect their browsing experience on the website. Cookies are computer files or partial data that can be stored on your computer or other Internet-enabled devices (e.g. smartphones or tablets) when you visit a website. A cookie contains the name of the website it comes from, the duration of the cookie (i.e. how long it will remain on your device) and a value that is usually a randomly generated unique number. Cookies are used to facilitate the use of the website and/or to tailor the website and the services offered to the user's interests and needs. Cookies can also be used to speed up the user's future activities on the website. Cookies are also used to track users and compile anonymous statistics in aggregate form.

More information about the cookies used.
When you visit this website, the following four types of cookies may be placed on your computer or device:
first-party cookies,
third-party cookies,
session cookies,
and persistent cookies.

Session cookies
The period of time between opening and closing your Internet browser is called a browsing session.
Session cookies are cookies stored on your computer or other device during a browsing session, but they expire and are normally deleted at the end of the browsing session.

First-party cookies
First-party cookies are cookies that are stored directly on the user's computer or other device. They may include cookies such as session cookies and persistent cookies (described below).
We use proprietary (first-party) cookies to track the movements of the computer or other device of the visitor who consults one of our sites, for example for analysis purposes.

Third-party cookies
Third-party cookies are cookies managed by third parties that may collect and track certain browsing data. This site uses the Google Analytics service (described in the browsing data and statistics collected by third parties). Persistent cookies are cookies stored on the visitor's computer or other device during a browsing session, but remain on the computer or other device after the end of that browsing session (e.g. password registration).
Persistent cookies allow our websites to recognise the visitor's computer or other device when it is used to access one of our websites again, after the end of a browsing session and at the start of a new browsing session, essentially to help the visitor quickly reconnect to our website.

Browsing data and statistics collected by third parties
As is now customary on the Internet, this site uses statistical analysis tools provided and managed by third parties that may collect and track certain browsing data.
It is worth noting that many Italian and foreign websites normally use these technologies and outsourced solutions, but very few mention this in their privacy policies. We have tried to do so and to inform you in the most accurate and transparent way possible: in any case, we are always at your disposal. As this data is collected by tools and companies other than the website operator, it is not physically owned by flow-otter.com, which can only use it for consultation purposes but cannot modify or delete it independently. For these operations and to learn more about the privacy policy applied to such data, the user must contact the Data Controller directly, i.e. the company that directly provides the statistical service used. The third-party tools used within this site are as follows: - Google Analytics (provided by: Google Inc. 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway - Mountain View CA 94043, USA).

Information about Google Analytics.
This website uses Google Analytics, a web analytics service provided by Google, Inc. (Google). Google Analytics uses cookies, which are text files placed on your computer to help the website analyse how users use the site.
The information generated by the cookie about your use of the website (including your IP address) will be transmitted to and stored by Google on servers in the United States. Google will use this information for the purpose of evaluating your use of the website, compiling reports on website activity for website operators and providing other services relating to website activity and internet usage. Google may also transfer this information to third parties where required to do so by law, or where such third parties process the information on Google's behalf. Google will not associate your IP address with any other data held by Google. You may refuse the use of cookies by selecting the appropriate settings on your browser, but this may prevent you from using all the features of this website. By using this website, you consent to the processing of data about you by Google in the manner and for the purposes set out above. Useful links for a better understanding of Google Analytics' privacy policy: - http://www.google.com/analytics/it-IT/tos.html - http://www.google.com/privacypolicy.html . Any requests regarding the data subject to this processing must be addressed to the Data Controller (Google Inc.).
privacy.section8:
Disclosure of personal data

Your personal data will not be shared with third parties, except for external auditors and professional advisors such as banking, legal, accounting and insurance advisors, as well as administrative, regulatory and law enforcement agencies. In addition, if the requested activity requires the involvement of an external inspector or collaborator, the data may be shared with the latter.
We require all third parties to respect the security of your personal data and to handle it in accordance with applicable law.
We do not allow third-party service providers to use your personal data for their own purposes, but we do allow them to process your personal data only for the specified purposes and in accordance with our instructions.
privacy.section9:
Data security

We have taken appropriate security measures to prevent the accidental loss of your personal data, as well as its use or access by unauthorised parties, and its alteration or dissemination. Furthermore, access to your personal data is limited to employees and other third parties who, for reasons related to the performance of their duties, need to know it. Your personal data will be processed exclusively on our instructions, and these individuals are bound by confidentiality obligations.
We have established procedures for handling any personal data breaches and will notify you and the relevant supervisory authority of any such breaches, if required by law.
privacy.section10:
Third-party links

This site may include links to third-party sites, as well as third-party plug-ins and applications (e.g. Facebook). By clicking on these links or connecting to them, you agree to third parties collecting or sharing your data. Third-party sites are not controlled by us, and flow-otter.com is not responsible for their privacy policies.
When leaving our site, you should read the privacy policy of any other site you visit.
privacy.section11:
Data retention

We will retain your personal data only for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes for which it was collected, including any legal, accounting or reporting requirements.
In order to determine the appropriate retention period for personal data, we consider the amount, nature and sensitivity of the personal data, the potential risk of harm from unauthorised use or disclosure of your personal data, the purposes for which we process your personal data and whether we have any alternative means of processing your personal data, together with applicable legal obligations. For tax purposes, the law requires us to retain basic information about our customers (including contact details, identification details, financial details and transactions) for ten years from the time the customer's status becomes invalid. CVs submitted via the relevant section of our website are retained for a maximum of 24 months, after which they are deleted from our database. In certain circumstances, you may ask us to delete data relating to you; for further information, please see the section on your legal rights below.
privacy.section12:
Rights guaranteed by law

The European General Data Protection Regulation applies to you, as you are the holder of the rights granted by privacy protection legislation in relation to your personal data.

Right to information - we are obliged to inform you about how our company uses your personal data (an obligation we comply with in accordance with this privacy policy);
Right of access - the right to submit a Data Subject Access Request to obtain a copy of the personal data stored by flow-otter.com;
Right to rectification - the right to request the correction of personal data if it is incomplete or incorrect;
Right to erasure - also known as the Right to be Forgotten when, in certain circumstances, you may request the deletion of personal data concerning you (provided that there is no overriding obligation to retain it);
Right to restriction of processing - the right to request, in certain circumstances, the suspension of the processing of personal data;
Right to portability - the right to request a copy of your personal data in a commonly used format (e.g., a .csv file);
Right to object – the right to object to the processing of your personal data (for example, if you do not consent to the processing of your data for direct marketing purposes).

These rights are subject to certain rules governing their exercise. For more information, please refer to the Guide to the application of the European Regulation on the protection of personal data. You may contact us if you wish to exercise any of the above rights (see the Contact flow-otter.com section for a privacy enquiry). Access to your personal data (or the exercise of the above rights) is free of charge. However, we reserve the right to charge a fee if the request is clearly unfounded, repetitive or excessive. Alternatively, in such circumstances, we may refuse to comply with your request. We may request specific information from you to help us confirm your identity and ensure proper access to your personal data (or to exercise any of your rights).
This security measure is necessary to ensure that personal data is not disclosed to third parties who are not entitled to receive it. We may also contact you to request further information regarding your request in order to expedite the process. We do our best to respond to all legitimate requests within one month. Sometimes it may take longer than a month if the request is particularly complex or if you have made numerous requests. In such cases, we will communicate the timeframe to you and keep you updated. If you have any further questions regarding this privacy policy or wish to submit a request to exercise any of your legal rights, you can contact the RDP Working Group using the contact details provided in section 14. How to contact flow-otter.com with privacy questions.
privacy.section13:
How to contact flow-otter.com with questions about privacy

If you have any questions about this privacy policy, or if you wish to exercise any of your rights, you can contact the Company in the following ways: Email: info@flow-otter.com.
